method.arithmetic: Parse timestamp_s, interval_start_s, and interval_end_s literals directly as exact decimals; compute widths, spacings, quantiles, and IQR without binary floating point.
method.dg075_dependence: DG-075 is the DG-071 distribution minus the first record: consecutive timestamp differences are the widths of records 2 through n up to the retained writer's endpoint convention.
method.float64_replication: A float64 replication (numpy `linear`, R type 7) is guaranteed to agree only to three decimals because a float64 at 1.78e9 s has spacing 2.4e-7 s, coarser than the file's 1e-7 s literals; the digits characterise the retained bytes, not the sampler's physical timing resolution. Worked example: median 120.9186 ms exact vs 120.9185 ms float64.
method.iqr: IQR is Q(0.75) - Q(0.25), computed exactly before rendering.
method.median: Median is the p = 0.5 quantile, the mean of the two middle values when n is even.
method.millisecond_rendering: Multiply exact seconds by 1000 and round to four decimal places with round-half-even; renderings are JSON strings.
method.population: A sampler record is one contiguous group sharing an exact timestamp_s literal. Each group has exactly one ane_power, cpu_power, and gpu_power row with byte-identical interval endpoint literals; one width per group enters DG-071.
method.quantile: Order n values ascending. At probability p, h = (n - 1) * p (0-based) and linearly interpolate exactly between the two neighbouring order statistics; this is Hyndman-Fan type 7 (numpy linear and R type 7 are cross-references).

DG-075.statistic: consecutive differences of sorted distinct timestamp_s literals
